title: Rational or radical equations and extraneous roots
subtitle: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  · 11 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **11 of the official questions in Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  are this one** — 2 Easy, 4 Medium, 5 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The variable sits under a square root or in a denominator, and the equation may include a constant with a stated sign.
- The question asks for 'the solution', 'one of the solutions', or a constant that leaves exactly one real solution.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) For fractions, multiply by the denominator, or cancel a common factor while noting the value x can't take.
- For radicals, isolate the root and square both sides.
- 3) Substitute each candidate into the original equation and throw out any that make a denominator zero or make the radical side negative.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph each side as its own curve and read off the intersections.
Extraneous roots simply won't show up, which makes this a reliable check against the squaring trap.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: That means a value that zeroes a denominator, or a squared-in solution where the square root would have to equal a negative number.
The wrong choices usually include exactly that value.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
That means a value that zeroes a denominator, or a squared-in solution where the square root would have to equal a negative number.
